picks.intervention_label: Larotrectinib (if NTRK1/2/3 fusion confirmed on RNA-based CGP)
picks.rationale: If the RNA fusion panel returns an NTRK fusion, this is the single largest response signal anywhere in the dossier: ORR 79% (95% CI 72-85), median DoR 35.2 months, median OS 44.4 months on pooled phase 1/2 data. Yes, NTRK fusions run under 1% in CCA, so the prior probability is low and the evidence is single-arm and pooled across tumor types. But the bet pays at a magnitude nothing else here touches, and the same paired panel that gates the FGFR2 and IDH1 calls returns this one at no extra cost. I rank it first on expected effect conditional on a positive read, not on prevalence.
primary_concerns: Sub-1% prevalence in CCA means the test is almost certainly negative, and a negative read drops this to zero.
Evidence is single-arm and pooled across many tumor types; no biliary-specific cohort and no randomized comparator.
Acquired resistance via NTRK kinase-domain mutations typically emerges, so the durable signal may not hold for every responder.

picks.intervention_label: Futibatinib (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
picks.rationale: FGFR2 fusion is the highest-yield axis to chase in intrahepatic CCA at roughly 10-15%, so this is the bet most likely to actually land. FOENIX-CCA2 showed ORR 42% (95% CI 32-52), median DoR 9.7 months, median OS 21.7 months, and only 2% discontinued for toxicity. The irreversible binding also holds up against several kinase-domain mutations that defeat pemigatinib, which buys a second move if the patient progresses. Single-arm phase 2 with an untested fusion is the honest limit here.
primary_concerns: Single-arm phase 2; the fusion is untested (ngs_pending) and subsite is unspecified at intake.
Hyperphosphatemia is near-universal on-target and reaches grade 3 in 30%, needing active phosphate management.
Eligibility was built on intrahepatic CCA, so a non-intrahepatic subsite weakens the match.

picks.intervention_label: Dabrafenib + trametinib (if BRAF V600E confirmed)
picks.rationale: The ROAR biliary cohort hit ORR 47% (95% CI 31-62) with median PFS 9.0 months, a strong number for a rare alteration sitting at 1-5%. A confirmed V600E gives two routes to treat, the CCA precedent and the tumor-agnostic label, so access is not the bottleneck. The cohort is small (n=43) and single-arm, and a VE1 IHC screen alone will not do; this needs NGS or PCR confirmation before anyone commits. Class-2/3 BRAF alterations do not qualify, so the test has to read true V600E.
primary_concerns: Small single-arm cohort (n=43); the mutation is untested.
Pyrexia is the characteristic combination effect and drove most treatment-related serious AEs at 21%.
A VE1 IHC screen is suggestive only; without NGS/PCR confirmation the V600E call is not actionable.

picks.intervention_label: Zanidatamab (if HER2 amplification/IHC-positive confirmed)
picks.rationale: HERIZON-BTC-01 returned a confirmed ORR 41.3% (95% CI 30.4-52.8) with median DoR 12.9 months, and the biparatopic design beat trastuzumab plus pertuzumab head-to-head in preclinical HER2 models, so the mechanistic case is stronger than a me-too antibody. HER2 skews toward extrahepatic and gallbladder disease, and subsite is unknown here, which is the real uncertainty. The gate is HER2 IHC with reflex ISH, not the DNA panel alone, so the workup has to include the protein readout. Watch the 3% grade-3 ejection-fraction drop given no baseline cardiac data was supplied.
primary_concerns: HER2 status is untested and needs IHC plus reflex ISH, not NGS copy-number alone.
Single-arm phase 2b; HER2 prevalence depends on a subsite that is unspecified at intake.
Decreased ejection fraction is a HER2-directed class effect and no baseline cardiac function was supplied.

picks.intervention_label: Ivosidenib (if IDH1 R132 confirmed)
picks.rationale: This is the one randomized phase 3 in the set (ClarIDHy, PFS HR 0.37, p<0.0001), and IDH1 R132 is common in intrahepatic CCA at 15-20%, so the bet is likely to land and the evidence is the cleanest here. What keeps it last for me is the thin absolute payoff: median PFS 2.7 vs 1.4 months and ORR just 2%, so the win is disease stabilization rather than tumor shrinkage. The preclinical mouse work suggests the real action may be immune-mediated and that ivosidenib synergizes with CTLA-4 blockade, which is the more interesting upside to chase in a trial. Strong evidence, modest single-agent effect.
primary_concerns: Absolute single-agent benefit is small (mPFS 2.7 vs 1.4 mo; ORR 2%) despite the strong hazard ratio.
IDH1 hotspot is untested (ngs_pending).
OS read was confounded by 70% placebo-to-ivosidenib crossover, leaving the survival case unsettled.

notes: Scope-unknown CCA, every feature ngs_pending: comprehensive genomic profiling is the rank-1 gating workup and all five picks are conditional on a positive confirmatory test, the RNA fusion panel plus DNA NGS plus HER2 IHC/ISH plus MMR/MSI. I deliberately ranked on expected effect size conditional on a positive read rather than on prevalence, which is why larotrectinib leads despite sub-1% frequency. I left pembrolizumab (MSI-H ORR 34.3%, TMB-high ORR 29%), NTRK-alternative entrectinib, RET selpercatinib, and KRAS G12C adagrasib off the ranked five; all are defensible if their feature tests positive, but their effect-size-times-prevalence case sits below my top five and the panel resolves them in the same pass. Risk posture: chase the biggest signal the test can unlock, accept that most reads come back negative, and re-rank hard the moment real molecular results land.

picks.intervention_label: Ivosidenib (if IDH1 R132 confirmed on tumor NGS)
picks.rationale: If the IDH1 hotspot reads positive, this is the one option in the set built on a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 (ClarIDHy, PFS HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.25-0.54), and its safety read is the reason it leads my list rather than its effect size. Grade 3+ events tracked placebo almost exactly: ascites 7% in both arms, no treatment-related deaths, and QT prolongation the one class effect, manageable with scheduled ECGs. I will be candid that the single-agent payoff is modest, with mPFS 2.7 vs 1.4 months and ORR only 2%, so I am buying disease control with a predictable toxicity bill rather than tumor shrinkage. IDH1 R132 sits at 15-20% in intrahepatic CCA, so among the candidate features this is also one of the likelier positives.
primary_concerns: IDH1 R132 is untested (ngs_pending); the whole pick collapses on a negative NGS read.
Absolute single-agent benefit is small (mPFS 2.7 vs 1.4 mo, ORR 2%), so the realistic goal is stabilization.
QT prolongation is a known class effect and needs baseline plus on-treatment ECG monitoring, which no organ-function labs at intake confirm is feasible.

picks.intervention_label: Pemigatinib (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
picks.rationale: On a confirmed FGFR2 fusion I reach for pemigatinib before the other FGFR agents because it carries the longest post-approval safety record, having been the first FGFR inhibitor approved in this indication off FIGHT-202 (ORR 35.5%, 95% CI 26.5-45.4). The on-target hyperphosphatemia ran 55% any-grade with no grade 3-4 events, and it has a well-rehearsed management ladder of phosphate binders, diet, and dose holds; serous retinal detachment at 4% is the item that needs scheduled ophthalmologic checks. I rank it above futibatinib on the toxicity axis specifically: futibatinib's grade 3 hyperphosphatemia reached 30%, against essentially none here, even if its ORR is nominally higher at 42%. FGFR2 fusions run 10-15% in intrahepatic CCA, so this is a feature worth testing for in earnest.
primary_concerns: FGFR2 fusion is untested (ngs_pending), and subsite is unspecified at intake; eligibility was built on intrahepatic disease.
Single-arm phase 2 with no randomized comparator, so the effect estimate carries the usual single-arm optimism.
Serous retinal detachment (4%) and nail/skin toxicity demand a monitoring schedule that the absent baseline data cannot yet confirm is in place.

picks.intervention_label: Larotrectinib (if NTRK1/2/3 fusion confirmed on RNA-based CGP)
picks.rationale: If the fusion panel returns an NTRK fusion, larotrectinib offers the gentlest grade 3+ profile of anything in the dossier: grade 3 events in 13% and grade 4 in under 1% across a 260-patient safety population, with no treatment-related deaths. That clean tolerability is what earns it a top-three slot from me even though the prevalence is under 1% and the evidence is single-arm pooled across tumor types with no biliary-specific cohort. The responses are also durable (mDoR 35.2 months), so a true positive buys real time at low toxicity cost. The same RNA panel that gates FGFR2 returns this at no added procedure.
primary_concerns: Sub-1% prevalence in CCA means the test almost certainly comes back negative.
Single-arm, pooled across tumor types; no randomized comparator and no biliary subgroup.
Acquired NTRK kinase-domain resistance mutations are documented, so durability is not guaranteed for every responder.

picks.intervention_label: Dabrafenib + trametinib (if BRAF V600E confirmed on NGS/PCR)
picks.rationale: A confirmed BRAF V600E opens a doublet whose toxicity I know cold from years of melanoma and other tumor-agnostic use, which matters more to me than the headline ORR of 47% (95% CI 31-62) in the ROAR biliary cohort. Pyrexia is the signature combination effect and drove the treatment-related serious AEs at 21%, but it has a standard playbook of dose interruption and antipyretics, and there were no treatment-related deaths. I hold it at rank 4 rather than higher because the cohort is small at n=43 and single-arm, and because the test has to read a true V600E on NGS or PCR; a VE1 IHC screen alone or a class 2/3 BRAF alteration does not qualify. That confirmation requirement is a hard gate, not a preference.
primary_concerns: Small single-arm cohort (n=43); the mutation is untested.
Pyrexia recurs as the characteristic combination toxicity and accounted for most treatment-related serious AEs (21%).
Actionable only on a true V600E confirmed by NGS/PCR; IHC alone and class 2/3 alterations do not gate the doublet.

picks.intervention_label: Zanidatamab (if HER2 IHC 3+ with reflex ISH confirmed)
picks.rationale: On confirmed HER2 positivity zanidatamab posted a confirmed ORR of 41.3% (95% CI 30.4-52.8) with mDoR 12.9 months in HERIZON-BTC-01, and I prefer it within the HER2 lane over trastuzumab deruxtecan on a straightforward safety argument: T-DXd carried 10.5% adjudicated ILD with three treatment-related deaths, an uncharacterized long-tail I am unwilling to take on without dedicated mitigation. Zanidatamab's grade 3 ejection-fraction drop sat at 3%, a familiar HER2-directed cardiac signal with an established baseline-and-serial-echo monitoring algorithm. I keep it at rank 5 because this is accelerated-approval, single-arm phase 2b evidence and because HER2 skews toward extrahepatic and gallbladder disease, so a positive read depends on a subsite that intake never specified. The gate is HER2 IHC with reflex ISH, not the DNA copy-number call alone.
primary_concerns: HER2 status is untested and requires IHC plus reflex ISH, not NGS copy-number alone.
Single-arm phase 2b accelerated approval; HER2 prevalence hinges on a subsite that intake did not specify.
Decreased ejection fraction is a class effect (3% grade 3) and no baseline cardiac function was supplied, so monitoring feasibility is unconfirmed.

notes: Scope-unknown CCA, every candidate feature ngs_pending: comprehensive genomic profiling is the rank-1 gating workup and all five picks are conditional on a positive confirmatory test (RNA fusion panel, DNA NGS covering IDH1/BRAF/KRAS hotspots, HER2 IHC with reflex ISH, and MMR/MSI). I ranked on evidence quality and safety characterization rather than raw effect size, which is why ivosidenib leads on the strength of the one randomized phase 3 and a near-placebo toxicity profile, and why pemigatinib outranks futibatinib despite a lower ORR. I deliberately left trastuzumab deruxtecan off the ranked five: its 10.5% adjudicated ILD with three treatment-related deaths is exactly the kind of uncharacterized severe AE I deprioritize absent dedicated combination/mitigation data, and zanidatamab covers the HER2 lane more safely. Selpercatinib (56% grade 3+, 7% grade-5 TEAEs), entrectinib, adagrasib (KRYSTAL-1 biliary n=12, ROBINS-I Serious), and pembrolizumab (MSI-H/TMB-high) are all defensible if their feature tests positive, but their safety characterization or evidence base sits below my top five; the panel resolves them in the same pass. If real molecular results, prior lines, performance status, or organ-function labs arrive, re-run intake; the ranking narrows hard to whichever feature reads positive.

picks.intervention_label: Ivosidenib (if IDH1 R132 confirmed on tumor NGS)
picks.rationale: This is the only intervention in the dossier that earns a top rank on evidence quality alone: ClarIDHy is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3, RoB2 rated Low, with the registered PFS primary endpoint met (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.25-0.54, p<0.0001). Everything else here is single-arm. I want to be exact about what it does and does not show: ORR was 2%, the realistic effect is delayed progression rather than shrinkage, and the OS story is unsettled because the intention-to-treat OS HR 0.69 (p=0.060) did not cross the conventional threshold. The 0.46 figure people quote is a model-based RPSFT crossover adjustment after 70% of placebo patients crossed over, so treat it as a sensitivity analysis, not the result.
primary_concerns: RoB2: outcome-blinding for PFS in an open-label-symptom disease is the residual domain to scrutinize, though independent review mitigates it.
ITT OS was not significant at the pre-specified alpha (HR 0.69, p=0.060); the 0.46 is crossover-adjusted modeling, not a clean survival result.
IDH1 R132 is untested (ngs_pending); the entire pick is conditional on the NGS read.

picks.intervention_label: Futibatinib (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
picks.rationale: Among the single-arm options this is the one I trust most, because the FGFR2-fusion axis carries something close to replication: two independent single-arm phase 2 trials (FOENIX-CCA2 and FIGHT-202) converge on the same effect direction in centrally confirmed fusions. FOENIX reported ORR 42% (95% CI 32-52) with median OS 21.7 months and only 2% discontinuing for toxicity. The hard limitation is that the registered primary endpoint is ORR, a surrogate, with no randomized comparator and no OS control arm. I rank it above pemigatinib because the central fusion confirmation and the activity against some pemigatinib-resistant kinase-domain mutations are documented in the trial, not extrapolated.
primary_concerns: Single-arm design with a surrogate primary endpoint (ORR); no comparator, so the response rate carries the usual single-arm inflation.
FGFR2 fusion is untested (ngs_pending) and the eligibility was built on intrahepatic CCA, while subsite is unspecified at intake.
Open-label response ascertainment; independent central review reduces but does not remove the bias.

picks.intervention_label: Pemigatinib (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
picks.rationale: FIGHT-202 is the second independent single-arm read on the FGFR2-fusion axis, ORR 35.5% (95% CI 26.5-45.4), and that concordance with FOENIX is what keeps the FGFR2 lane near the top of my list rather than the individual numbers. The same caveats as futibatinib apply in full: single-arm, ORR surrogate, accelerated approval rather than a confirmed survival endpoint. The reported OS of 21.1 months is explicitly immature, 40 events at cutoff, so I would not lean on it. I place it just below futibatinib because the head-to-head evidence does not exist and futibatinib at least documents activity in the post-pemigatinib resistance setting.
primary_concerns: Single-arm phase 2, surrogate ORR endpoint, accelerated approval; the OS estimate is immature (40 events).
FGFR2 fusion is untested (ngs_pending); subsite unspecified at intake.
Selective-reporting risk is low but the lack of a comparator means no protection against regression-to-mean in the response estimate.

picks.intervention_label: Zanidatamab (if HER2 IHC 3+ with reflex ISH confirmed)
picks.rationale: HERIZON-BTC-01 gives a confirmed ORR of 41.3% (95% CI 30.4-52.8) with median DoR 12.9 months, and unlike the basket cohorts it is a dedicated biliary trial, which is why it outranks the HER2 alternatives on my list. The evidence is still single-arm phase 2b on a surrogate endpoint behind an accelerated approval, so I hold it at rank 4. The gate is HER2 IHC with reflex ISH using the trial's own scoring, not breast or gastric thresholds and not an NGS copy-number call substituting for the protein read. HER2 skews extrahepatic and gallbladder, so a positive result is conditional on a subsite intake never specified.
primary_concerns: Single-arm phase 2b, surrogate ORR endpoint, accelerated approval; no randomized comparator.
HER2 status is untested and requires IHC plus reflex ISH on the protocol's scoring, not NGS amplification alone.
Open-label response ascertainment; central review present but no comparator arm.

picks.intervention_label: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (if HER2 IHC 3+ confirmed) - listed to flag the subgroup problem
picks.rationale: I include T-DXd specifically to mark where the evidence gets weak, because the eye-catching 61.3% number is a post-hoc HER2 IHC 3+ subgroup, not the registered biliary-cohort result, which was ORR 22% (95% CI 10.6-37.6) on n=41. Unadjusted subgroup splits like this are exactly what I discount: the confidence interval on the full cohort is wide, the IHC 3+ slice is smaller still, and the response was investigator-assessed in the biliary cohort rather than independently reviewed. The defining safety signal is adjudicated drug-related ILD at 10.5% with three treatment-related deaths, and the AE rates are reported study-wide rather than for the biliary cohort. If forced to treat a HER2 case I would want zanidatamab's dedicated-trial data first and reserve T-DXd for a documented IHC 3+ read with explicit ILD monitoring.
primary_concerns: The 61.3% figure is a post-hoc unadjusted subgroup, not the pre-specified biliary-cohort endpoint (22%, 95% CI 10.6-37.6, n=41).
Investigator-assessed response in the biliary cohort and study-wide rather than cohort-specific safety reporting.
Adjudicated ILD 10.5% with three treatment-related deaths is the dominant risk, and no organ-function or pulmonary baseline was supplied at intake.

notes: Scope-unknown CCA, every feature ngs_pending: comprehensive genomic profiling is the rank-1 gating workup and all five picks are conditional on a positive confirmatory test. I ranked strictly on evidence quality by my lights. Ivosidenib leads because ClarIDHy is the lone randomized phase 3 (RoB2 Low), even though its absolute single-agent effect is small and its OS claim rests on crossover-adjusted modeling that did not reach significance in ITT. The FGFR2 pair (futibatinib then pemigatinib) sits next because two independent single-arm trials converging on the same axis is the closest thing to replication in this dossier, with the honest caveat that both ride a surrogate ORR endpoint with no comparator. Zanidatamab is the strongest HER2 read because it is a dedicated biliary trial rather than a basket. I deliberately listed T-DXd at rank 5 to flag, not to endorse: its quoted 61.3% is a post-hoc IHC 3+ subgroup, not the registered cohort result of 22%. Off the ranked five and weakest on my axis: pembrolizumab (no CCA-specific subgroup ORR published in KEYNOTE-158 for either the MSI-H or TMB-high read; the patient is admitted on the biomarker into a 27-tumor or pooled basket), dabrafenib+trametinib (single-arm n=43 basket), larotrectinib/entrectinib (pooled cross-tumor baskets, no biliary subgroup), selpercatinib (n=45 basket, 7% grade-5 TEAEs), and adagrasib (KRYSTAL-1 biliary n=12, ROBINS-I Serious - the single weakest evidence row in the set). Each is defensible only if its feature tests positive, and the same CGP pass resolves all of them. I have read the abstracts and compiled rows here, not the full protocols for every trial, so my RoB judgments on the single-arm studies rest on the design and reported endpoints, not on protocol-level inspection of analysis plans.

picks.intervention_label: Ivosidenib (if IDH1 R132 confirmed on tumor NGS)
picks.rationale: If the IDH1 hotspot reads positive, ivosidenib is the one option here that sits on a randomized phase 3 and converges across the bodies I track: NCCN Hepatobiliary/Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 lists it category 2A for subsequent-line IDH1-mutant disease, and ESMO's 2023 BTC update recommends it on the strength of ClarIDHy (PFS HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.25-0.54). I rank it first on guideline anchoring, not on tumor shrinkage, since ORR was only 2% and the realistic goal is delayed progression. IDH1 R132 also runs 15-20% in intrahepatic CCA, so among the candidate features it is one of the likelier positives the panel will return.
primary_concerns: IDH1 R132 is untested (ngs_pending); a negative NGS read voids the pick entirely.
Guidelines assume measurable progression and ECOG fit; intake supplied no organ-function labs and ECOG 1 is an assumption, so QT monitoring feasibility is unconfirmed.
The category 2A listing rests on a surrogate-weighted phase 3 whose ITT OS did not separate (HR 0.69, p=0.060), a point the consensus folds into the 2A rather than category 1 grade.

picks.intervention_label: Futibatinib (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
picks.rationale: On a confirmed FGFR2 fusion, futibatinib is NCCN BTC v2.2025 category 2A for subsequent-line disease and carries the higher ESMO-MCBS v1.1 score of the FGFR pair (3 for futibatinib versus 2 for pemigatinib), which is why I put it ahead of pemigatinib here. FOENIX-CCA2 reported ORR 42% (95% CI 32-52), median OS 21.7 months, and only 2% discontinued for toxicity. FGFR2 fusions sit at 10-15% in intrahepatic CCA, the highest-yield molecular axis to test for in this disease. The MCBS score is the cross-Atlantic tiebreaker; the US and European bodies otherwise agree on the indication.
primary_concerns: FGFR2 fusion is untested (ngs_pending); the guideline indication is built on intrahepatic CCA and subsite is unspecified at intake, so a non-intrahepatic primary weakens the fit.
Category 2A here reflects single-arm phase 2 data with a surrogate ORR endpoint, not a randomized survival comparison.
On-target hyperphosphatemia reaches grade 3 in 30% and needs active phosphate management the guideline assumes is available.

picks.intervention_label: Pemigatinib (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
picks.rationale: Pemigatinib is the other guideline-endorsed FGFR2 option, NCCN BTC v2.2025 category 2A and ESMO-recommended off FIGHT-202 (ORR 35.5%, 95% CI 26.5-45.4), and it has the longest post-approval track record in the indication as the first FGFR inhibitor approved for CCA. I place it just below futibatinib because its ESMO-MCBS v1.1 score is 2 against futibatinib's 3 and futibatinib documents activity against some pemigatinib-resistant kinase-domain mutations, which matters for sequencing. Both share the same FGFR2-fusion gate, so the choice between them is a within-lane call once the fusion is confirmed. The two trials converging on the same axis is what gives the consensus its confidence.
primary_concerns: FGFR2 fusion is untested (ngs_pending); subsite unspecified at intake against an intrahepatic-built indication.
Single-arm phase 2 behind an accelerated approval; the reported OS of 21.1 months is immature at 40 events.
Serous retinal detachment (4%) requires the scheduled ophthalmologic monitoring the guideline presumes is feasible, unconfirmed here.

picks.intervention_label: Zanidatamab (if HER2 IHC 3+ with reflex ISH confirmed)
picks.rationale: Zanidatamab was added to NCCN BTC v2.2025 as a category 2A subsequent-line option for HER2-positive disease after its accelerated approval off HERIZON-BTC-01 (confirmed ORR 41.3%, 95% CI 30.4-52.8, median DoR 12.9 months). I rank it as the lead HER2 choice because it is the only dedicated biliary HER2 trial behind a guideline listing, where T-DXd enters BTC through a pan-tumor basket. The gate the guideline assumes is HER2 IHC with reflex ISH on the trial's own scoring, not a breast or gastric cutoff and not an NGS copy-number call standing in for the protein read. HER2 skews toward extrahepatic and gallbladder disease, so a positive result depends on a subsite intake never specified.
primary_concerns: HER2 status is untested and requires IHC plus reflex ISH, not NGS amplification alone, to meet the guideline's gating definition.
The category 2A rests on single-arm phase 2b accelerated-approval data with no randomized comparator.
HER2 prevalence hinges on a subsite intake left blank, and no baseline cardiac function was supplied for the 3% grade-3 ejection-fraction signal.

picks.intervention_label: Dabrafenib + trametinib (if BRAF V600E confirmed on NGS/PCR)
picks.rationale: A confirmed BRAF V600E gives a doublet that both NCCN BTC v2.2025 (category 2A, subsequent-line) and the tumor-agnostic FDA label endorse, with the ROAR biliary cohort showing ORR 47% (95% CI 31-62) and median PFS 9.0 months. The cross-society and cross-label convergence is real, but I hold it at rank 5 because V600E appears in only about 1-5% of BTC and the cohort is small (n=43) and single-arm. The guideline gate is a true V600E on NGS or PCR; a VE1 IHC screen alone or a class 2/3 BRAF alteration does not qualify. Pyrexia is the signature combination effect and has a standard dose-hold and antipyretic playbook the consensus assumes is in place.
primary_concerns: BRAF V600E is untested (ngs_pending); only a confirmed V600E on NGS/PCR meets the guideline gate, IHC alone and class 2/3 alterations do not.
Category 2A here rests on a small single-arm basket cohort (n=43).
Pyrexia drove the treatment-related serious AEs at 21% and needs the monitoring the guideline presumes, unconfirmed against absent baseline data.

notes: Scope-unknown CCA, every candidate feature ngs_pending: comprehensive genomic profiling is the rank-1 gating workup and all five picks are conditional on a positive confirmatory test (RNA fusion panel, DNA NGS over IDH1/BRAF/KRAS hotspots, HER2 IHC with reflex ISH, MMR/MSI). I ranked on guideline endorsement and cross-society convergence rather than raw effect size. Ivosidenib leads because it is the one randomized phase 3 with both NCCN BTC v2.2025 category 2A and ESMO 2023 backing; the FGFR2 pair follows with futibatinib ahead of pemigatinib on the higher ESMO-MCBS v1.1 score (3 vs 2). Zanidatamab is the guideline-endorsed HER2 lead (NCCN 2A, dedicated biliary trial) over basket-route T-DXd, and dab+tram rounds out the five on NCCN 2A plus the tumor-agnostic label. Off the ranked five but guideline-endorsed if their feature tests positive: pembrolizumab (NCCN-listed for MSI-H/dMMR and TMB-high via tumor-agnostic labels, though KEYNOTE-158 reports no CCA-specific subgroup ORR), larotrectinib/entrectinib (NTRK, tumor-agnostic), and selpercatinib (RET, tumor-agnostic). I left adagrasib for KRAS G12C off because the biliary readout is a 12-patient cohort (ROBINS-I Serious) and no society lists a BTC-specific KRAS G12C recommendation yet; trial enrollment is the guideline-aligned route there. Every NCCN category cited is 2A because none of these options reaches category 1 in BTC, a point worth flagging: the consensus has calibrated the same single-arm and surrogate-driven evidence the critic reads, and 2A is where it landed. If real molecular results, prior lines, performance status, or organ-function labs arrive, re-run intake; the ranking narrows to whichever feature reads positive.

picks.intervention_label: Ivosidenib (if IDH1 R132 confirmed on tumor NGS)
picks.rationale: With the patient's own efficacy/toxicity weight set at a balanced 0.5, this is the cleanest fit on the board: a once-daily oral pill whose grade 3+ toxicity ran about the same as placebo in the only randomized phase-3 trial here (ClarIDHy, PFS HR 0.37). Nobody told us this patient minds infusions, but a drug that reads like placebo on safety respects a balanced weight better than anything else conditional on a positive test. The lone real preference on file, prefers_trials, is honored too, since the open registration trial (NCT02989857) is the trial route to the same drug. The catch is the gate itself: IDH1 R132 lands in maybe 15-20% of intrahepatic disease, so this only matters if the NGS comes back positive.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: balanced efficacy/toxicity weight (oral, placebo-like grade 3+ profile) and prefers_trials (open phase-3 registration trial).
Conditional on IDH1 R132, untested here (ngs_pending); the whole pick collapses if the hotspot is wild-type.
OS signal was diluted by 70% placebo crossover, so the magnitude of survival benefit is softer than the PFS number alone suggests.

picks.intervention_label: Futibatinib (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed on RNA-based CGP)
picks.rationale: FGFR2 fusion is the highest-yield molecular axis in this disease (roughly 10-15% of intrahepatic cases), and futibatinib is oral, continuous, and easy to hand a patient who has stated no modality limits. Only 2% of patients came off FOENIX-CCA2 for treatment-related toxicity, which sits well with the balanced weight; hyperphosphatemia is the on-target effect to watch but stayed manageable (ORR 42%, 95% CI 32-52). Because prefers_trials is the one preference actually on file, I would surface the FGFR2 trial menu in the same breath, including the next-generation TYRA-200 study (NCT06160752) for anyone who later progresses on a first FGFR inhibitor. Same proviso as everywhere on this board: it rides entirely on a confirmed fusion the NGS has not yet returned.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: balanced weight (low 2% discontinuation, oral) and prefers_trials (active FGFR2 trials including a resistance-directed option).
Conditional on an RNA-based fusion call; DNA-only panels can miss FGFR2 fusions, so the test method itself matters here.
Single-arm phase-2 evidence (tier 2b), no randomized comparator.

picks.intervention_label: Larotrectinib (if NTRK1/2/3 fusion confirmed on RNA-based CGP)
picks.rationale: If the fusion panel turns up NTRK, this is the option I would push hardest for the patient: an oral drug with the most durable responses among the tumor-agnostic agents (ORR 79%, 95% CI 72-85) and a notably light toxicity profile (grade 3 AEs in 13%, grade 4 under 1%). That combination of high response and low burden is exactly what a 0.5 efficacy/toxicity weight is asking for. An open basket trial (NCT02576431) also satisfies prefers_trials. The honest limit is prevalence: NTRK fusions sit under 1% in biliary cancer, so the expected value is small until the RNA panel says otherwise.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: balanced weight (oral, low grade 3+ rate, durable responses) and prefers_trials.
Conditional on a rare (<1%) NTRK fusion best caught by RNA-based testing, not DNA panels.
Pooled phase-1/2 data across mixed tumor types, no CCA-specific cohort.

picks.intervention_label: Pembrolizumab (if MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high confirmed)
picks.rationale: For an MSI-H or TMB-high tumor, immunotherapy can deliver the long tail of durable response that chemo never does, and treatment-related grade 3-5 events stayed at 14.6% in KEYNOTE-158. It is given IV every three weeks rather than as a pill, but preferences.json states no modality constraint, so I am not going to invent one and downgrade it on a route the patient never objected to. The same comprehensive panel that resolves the other axes also returns MSI and TMB, so this costs no extra biopsy. A biomarker-selected basket trial (NCT02628067) covers the prefers_trials preference; the caveat is that MSI-H is rare in biliary cancer (roughly 1-3%).
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: prefers_trials (open MSI-H/TMB-high basket). In tension only on an axis the patient left blank: IV modality, which I am not treating as a veto because none was stated.
Conditional on MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high, both rare in this disease.
No CCA-specific subgroup ORR was reported, so the biliary-specific magnitude is inferred from the basket.

picks.intervention_label: Dabrafenib + trametinib (if BRAF V600E confirmed on NGS)
picks.rationale: Oral, tumor-agnostic, and active in the ROAR biliary cohort (ORR 47%, 95% CI 31-62), so it clears the modality and trial preferences without trouble. Where I would slow down for this patient is the tolerability half of the balanced weight: pyrexia hit 19% and serious AEs reached 40%, which is a heavier load than ivosidenib or the FGFR inhibitors carry. I am not vetoing it, because the patient set no fever or hospitalization veto, but a balanced weight means this ranks below the gentler oral options rather than above them. BRAF V600E is uncommon here (1-5%), so this stays a contingency pending the NGS.
primary_concerns: Satisfied: oral modality and prefers_trials (open BRAF basket, NCT02034110).
In tension with the tolerability side of the 0.5 weight: 40% serious AE rate and frequent pyrexia, heavier than the higher-ranked oral agents.
